symptom: `rename snippet M.X to Y` was a syntax error, `mxcli rename page M.X Y` on a snippet said page not found, and `mxcli syntax rename` listed no snippet target — while CONV005 tells users to rename snippets to SNIPPET_*.
cause: renameTarget in MDLParser.g4 had no SNIPPET, and execRename/renameDocType/the CLI renameTypes table had no snippet case. Everything underneath already handled snippets: the name-space clash rule (pages/snippets/layouts share one), the alter-target listing, and RenameReferences, since a snippet call names its snippet by qualified name.
fix: SNIPPET added to renameTarget, execRename routes it to execRenameDocument with a snippet listing, renameDocType maps it, the CLI and the syntax topic list it, CONV005's suggestion prints the statement.
insight: A missing doctype in a dispatch is cheap when the layers below are generic — check what the shared pieces (clash rule, target listing, by-name sweep) already know before writing per-type code. Probe exec's refusal before adding a duplicate check: the cross-kind name clash was already exec-enforced.
test: mdl/executor/rename_snippet_2130_pedapp_test.go (page and nested snippet calls follow; dry run changes nothing; refusals: missing snippet, taken snippet name, taken page name); before the change the statement did not parse
